titleEn: If Grandma Didn't Give It to Me, I Won't Eat It!

pages.text: "Wow, so round!" Dingding picked a berry from the grass on the bank. Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, was pulling weeds farther ahead. Dingding lifted the berry right up to their nose.
"It's a long time until our meal, and I'm hungry." Dingding rolled the berry between both hands and started to put it into their mouth. "This will stop me being hungry, won't it?"
"No, Dingding!" Grandma hurried over and held Dingding's hand. "Neither of us knows what that is." Startled, Dingding stopped moving their hand.
Grandma took roasted beans from the bamboo basket and put them on Dingding's palm. "What Grandma gives you is safe to eat." Dingding crunched the beans. They tasted nutty!
Grandma pointed at the berries with a stick. "Eating something you don't know can make your tummy as cloudy as muddy water." Dingding imagined murky water.
"One, put unknown things down! Two, don't put them in your mouth! Three, ask a grown-up!" Grandma sang, "If Grandma Didn't Give It to Me, I Won't Eat It!" Dingding put the berry back in the grass.

A little later, a round white mushroom stood in the shade of the bank grass. Dingding tucked their hands behind their back. "If Grandma Didn't Give It to Me, I Won't Eat It!" Then Dingding ran to Grandma.

Grandma looked closely and shook her head. "That's a mushroom, but eating it would hurt your tummy." Dingding sniffed. It had no smell. "Good thing I asked!" Dingding opened the hands they had hidden.
Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, arrived with the meal on her head. Dingding told her first. "One, put it down! Two, don't put it in my mouth! Three, ask!" Mom's eyes widened.

Grandma held Dingding's hand and rubbed her cheek against theirs. "You stopped just before it reached your mouth. Well done." Ask a grown-up before putting unknown things in your mouth. Dingding ate a roasted bean. "If Grandma Didn't Give It to Me, I Won't Eat It!"
